output.brief: The evidence points mainly at Callerby, not Halden. The shared platform's tamper-proof timestamps show the architect answered 62 of 64 information requests within the contract period. The 41 requests the claim calls late mostly sat in Callerby's own draft folder for 9–47 days before being submitted. Our crane went to Kestrel in October 2025 and did not return until April. The frame was recorded as "on hold – design" the whole time, and the steel was on the ground. Steel erection restarted in April, when the crane came back. It did not restart when the last change order was issued on 9 December. How much delay the change orders caused is still unclear. Halden calls them small, but CO-09 did add steel. Submitting the claim as drafted would put an inaccurate analysis in front of Halden. It would also invite a counter-claim, and the claims consultant earns a percentage of any recovery. Do not submit it on 1 December. Do not discipline the superintendent, who told the truth. Do not suspend the incentive scheme on this evidence. Have an independent analyst check what the change orders actually held up, then decide whether to submit a reduced claim. This is moderately confident, and the change-order share is the main open question.
